title: TRADE, TRAVEL, AND TOURISM COMMITTEE REPORT relative to requesting Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA) and the City Attorney to report on workforce…
text:
[Council File 26-1611; CD 6]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Been Held]
TRADE, TRAVEL, AND TOURISM COMMITTEE REPORT relative to requesting Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA) and the City Attorney to report on workforce development, community impacts, noise mitigation, infrastructure improvements, and lease policies at Van Nuys Airport (VNY).
Recommendations for Council action, pursuant to Motion (Padilla – Park):
1. REQUEST Los Angeles World Airports (LAWA), within 90 days, to submit a Van Nuys Airport (VNY) Jobs and Workforce Plan with baselines, numeric targets, dates, and annual reports, including:
a. A wage standard for jobs under future VNY leases, set at or above the Living Wage Ordinance airport employee rate, with employer health coverage, phased in on a stated schedule.
b. A written transition plan for every VNY tenant displaced or reduced by a pending lease, covering notice, relocation within VNY, and retention or placement of its workers.
c. Verified annual permanent and construction job counts by job type, wage band, and worker ZIP code.
d. First Source Hiring modeled on Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), with Women in Non- Traditional Employment Roles (WINTER) and school training partnerships, and at least 20 percent of construction labor hours for residents of nearby low-income ZIP codes and 15 percent apprentice hours.
2. REQUEST LAWA to submit to Council, within 120 days, a Good Neighbor Plan for the blocks nearest VNY, with targets reported biannually, covering:
a. A complaint line answered during published hours, with a response within one business day and a public complaint log.
b. Monthly public reporting of flight operations by hour, night operations, curfew violations, tower hours, complaints, and response times.
c. Independent air quality monitoring for ultrafine particles, fine particulate matter, nitrogen oxides, and lead along Hayvenhurst Avenue, with publicly available data.
3. REQUEST LAWA, as airport sponsor, to ask the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), within 90 days, to support and fund an update of the VNY Part 150 noise study, including its Noise Exposure Maps and Noise Compatibility Program, reflecting existing operations, detailed analysis supporting mitigation, and the location and nature of proposed elements for FAA consideration; and to report the FAA's response to Council within 60 days of receipt.
4. REQUEST LAWA, in coordination with the Department of City Planning, Board of Public Works, and Department of Transportation, to present a plan within 120 days for streetscape improvements at Sherman Way, Woodley, Roscoe, Valjean, Hayvenhurst, and Balboa, including lighting, public art, signage and wayfinding, intersection improvements, landscaping, and related amenities to enhance VNY's major gateways.
5. REQUEST LAWA to present, within 60 days, a draft VNY Lease Solicitation and Performance Policy, including its estimated effect on airport revenue, and to adopt the policy before issuing any new VNY request for proposals, before any Commissioner is seated under Charter Amendment PRT and the resulting Ordinance, and in any event within 90 days; and to publish scoring weights with every solicitation. The policy shall include:
a. Minimum requirements for electric ground power capacity; LEED Silver certification and performance 15 percent better than Title 24; a zero-emission ground equipment schedule; an unleaded fuel plan; Quieter Nights participation; and First Source Hiring.
b. Scoring criteria maintaining financial return as the largest category, with community improvements, workforce, and environmental criteria collectively accounting for at least 35 percent, including points for verified jobs, wages, and local hiring.
c. Revenue and enforcement provisions, including a minimum annual guarantee, percentage rent, scheduled rent resets, public annual reports, periodic independent audits, cure periods, and remedies.
6. REQUEST the City Attorney, in coordination with LAWA counsel, to report to Council within 45 days on which lease terms constitute tenant conduct versus access restrictions under federal noise law; whether the wage standard can bind VNY tenants; whether tenant community contributions constitute airport revenue; how hiring targets may be established based on residency and income; and whether the proposed policy requires an ordinance.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
